STEP 1 - Scene: A small snack of sliced fresh strawberries on a white square plate, photographed from directly above (overhead view).

STEP 2 - Ruler: White square plate, roughly 20 cm across (side plate size). Area ≈ 20 x 20 ≈ 400 cm^2 (square plate, so use side x side). Strawberry halves/quarters are about 3-4 cm across, which is consistent with this scale.

STEP 3 - Items: Sliced/halved fresh strawberries (about 7-8 pieces, a mix of halves and wedges). No sauce, cream or oil visible.

STEP 4 - Area: The berry pile covers roughly 20% of the plate area (~80 cm^2) in total.

STEP 5 - Volume: Pile of about 80 cm^2 with typical height ~2 cm gives ~160 ml gross volume.

STEP 6 - Grams: Cut fruit bulk density ~0.6 g/ml → 160 x 0.6 ≈ 96 g. Rounded to about 95 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Strawberries, raw ≈ 32 kcal/100 g → 95 g x 0.32 ≈ 30 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Seven or eight strawberry pieces totaling roughly 90-100 g is plausible (a whole strawberry is ~12-15 g, and the halves/wedges here sum to about that many whole berries). Energy of ~30 kcal is consistent with fresh strawberries. Estimate only what is visible.
